answer: New identities join in groups of twelve that insure one another. Each locks a 20-credit deposit into a pool, and every job one member finishes is checked by two others, since a fake that slips through burns everyone's deposit at once. Payments flow through the pool like a river, and every receipt sits in a crystal-clear ledger, so a copied job is visible to all twelve. When one member is proven fake, all 240 credits are slashed and the group dissolves, a gale that scatters the farm. A hundred fakes means nine fake-only pools and 2,000 credits at risk.
